title: Never bend content to pass a check
statement: Never alter an item, request or check just to raise a score: a gain from removing what a check inspects is gaming, so fix the item or harden the check.
example: An edit that disabled detection cut the findings from 28/12 to 15/8, a mix of real cleanup and switched-off checks.
detail: An audit of a Grade 5 course found that an uncommitted lint edit cut findings by weakening the gate: it replaced the total invariant with a condition that is always false, suppressed unit-split failures and broadened exemptions, so the drop from 28/12 to 15/8 was a mix of real cleanup and disabled detection that could not count as progress toward approval (`grade3-reading/artifacts/takeover-audit-2026-07-13/g5-clean-baseline.md`). An earlier fix had inserted a taught word into another lesson's closing page to pass a vocabulary check, and was reverted as editing someone else's lesson to satisfy the validator (`grade3-reading/artifacts/DECISIONS-2026-08-24.md`). A capstone lesson was named by the procedure its thinking fits, read from the procedures' definitions, because the nearest-sounding label would have been mislabelling to satisfy a validator (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/CAPSTONE-PROCEDURE-RULING-2026-08-18.md`), and a later review adjudicated 2-1 that another lesson's procedure label was wrong for a trace that related nothing, fixed by a one-line relabel (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-25-R10.md`). Fix content that fails a sound check rather than loosen the check, judge an expected-answer change by what it does for learners, and confirm that a fix that raises a score improved the item rather than dodged the check.
against: Content is sometimes bent to an engine on purpose, and then recorded as such: one candidate fix was called honest, but content bent to an engine (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-09-16-R25.md`). The relabel changed nothing a student sees, since the procedure value renders no visible chip (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-25-R10.md`). One check was itself wrong: an echo guard rejected a word-perfect recall of the taught sentence (0.74 against its 0.70 threshold), and the fix reworded the three criterion strings rather than the guard (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0229-closing-questions-build-2026-09-25.qmd`, lines 72-82). The rule covers only what the judge sees: post-processing outside its view, such as image generation, logging and transport retries, was ruled fine (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/research/inference_clean.md`, lines 414-415), and dropping a failed candidate was still allowed (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/PILLARS_2026_05_12.md`, line 64). The changed requests had a stated reason, that 'easy is misleading' for complex formats (the same audit, line 74), and the audit applied the project's single-attempt rule rather than measuring any loss of quality. It rests on one AP case, reported in a later synthesis rather than in the project's own records. The production pipeline took the trick up as a strategy: "PIL shipped 0.1.82-0.1.85 commits today integrating your stimulus-strip insight as a **prompt-design strategy** (no-stimulus LLM lane for MCQ when standard is specific). Direct adoption." (icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/inbox/2026-05-22T1910Z_T2_T3_T4_invitation.md, 14). The test's own report grants that items without a source have a place: "Many textbook drills and formative-assessment items omit stimuli for the same reason (faster recall practice)." (icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/exploits/EXPLOIT-002-stimulus-strip.md, 212-214), and its final report argued: "The structural exploits don't generate "fake" content — they generate REAL content shaped to bypass rubric-default checks." (icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/reports/FINAL_REPORT.md, 140-141)
